accepted_scope: Complete selected kernel-only Contract, exact-Real Correct and one-model native FPEquiv, including successful execution of the entire quoted grid, actual caller Tensor logical outputs, exterior/read-allocation frames and empty calls, within the explicitly declared observation/compiler/instruction/runtime boundaries.

canonical_selection.note: The current contract_revision selects the repaired source named above. Historical original-source defects and older separate-repair acceptance refer to other revisions. The reviewer did not update the ledger or canonical selection.

conclusion: The public endpoints derive complete source-grid success and every logical caller output from admission, ordinary Tensor laws and full-grid ordering. Neither endpoint assumes a successful run, supplied final output, arbitrary dot/reduction/attention result or whole-execution equality. The independent Real target and independently written native recurrence are connected to the unchanged shared DSL quotation. Current task build receipts, import closure, saved host/address/compiler/CPU controls and preservation claims are consistent. Acceptance is for the declared kernel scope, without a GPU, universal device-resource, universal compiler-conformance or native-to-Real accuracy certification.

source_and_contract_review.source_extent: The quotation covers the full selected _fwd_kernel_aligned body for FP16 and BF16: independent Q/K/V/Out pitches, block pointers, initialization, query scaling, static bias window, entire dynamic K/V loop, both dots, relative bias, key-tail mask, online maximum/normalizer/value update, pointer advances, final division and masked output store. kernelAs fixes P_SEQ=0 and bias parameters to the actual wrapper values.
source_and_contract_review.precision_annotations: The two typed bodies expose already-FP32 default dot results with a carrier .to(tl.float32), and expose the implicit scalar conversion of 1.44269504 to storage precision for bias arithmetic. Saved TTIR confirms the source casts and FP16/BF16 bias operations. These annotations neither replace the selected Python nor introduce a new numerical repair.
source_and_contract_review.admission: InputContract is derived from the shared Torch metadata, observed four-dimensional strides, original pointers and full allocation spans. The same shape/dtype/device/resolved-bit/scalar/configuration/bias checks apply before the empty return. Nonempty calls retain dense rows, independent nonoverlapping batch/head pitches, signed integer/grid-y limits, two-byte alignment, unsigned64 formed-address bounds and separation of output storage from every read storage. Input/input aliasing remains admitted. No finite tensor-payload restriction or stronger Python guard was added.
source_and_contract_review.ordinary_API_boundary: TensorLaws states capacity, coordinate-to-physicalIndex, in-bounds, nonempty pointer and bias last-dimension contiguity laws. It contains no execution, output, separation or floating-result promise. Exact Python type/scalar classification, truthful API observations and stable caller memory are explicit boundaries; no verified Python parser is claimed.
source_and_contract_review.scale_word: Call records both the Real scale interpretation and the actual observed FP32 launch word. FamilyNative.binaryWithScale uses that word at the scale-times-log2(e) syntax site, preserving signed zero. The scalar/JIT observation boundary is explicit and does not serve as an output premise.
source_and_contract_review.integer_and_address_closure: The original Machine.closed result is applied to parameters and bases extracted from the actual call. It covers padded formed offsets, bias columns, pointer advances and smaller nonnegative subexpressions, their signed32/signed64 representations, and unsigned64 physical address bounds. The shared grid-product compatibility question remains outside this task as declared.

complete_execution_review.operational_source: Whole.runPrograms executes FP.Structural.exec on Source.kernel at each submitted program and threads current memory to the remaining programs. Source.kernel selects the existing TypedSource.repaired quotation. source_memory proves full entry/loop/post success and the masked store state; it does not take full execution success as a premise.
complete_execution_review.full_grid: The grid is [ceil(N/BM), B*H, 1]. KernelOnly.complete derives source success for every permutation of all grid programs. grid_covers maps every logical output to a valid program/lane; grid_unique derives noncolliding stores from admitted dense-row and independent-pitch geometry. ReadsEq and the source frame preserve all later program inputs.
complete_execution_review.output_quantification: Correct.kernel_correct and FPEquiv.kernel_native quantify every b<B, h<H, n<N and d<D. Their existential final state is produced by the complete run; the corresponding output is read at the original caller Out pointer and Tensor physicalIndex. The source wrapper mutates caller-provided output and returns None; no newly allocated or copied output object is claimed.
complete_execution_review.empty_calls: For empty batch, head or context, no_grid derives an empty program list. Correct.empty_kernel proves identity source execution and unchanged caller word observations. It does not require the nonempty stride, pointer or allocation-separation guards.

independent_Real_review.mathematical_domain: The target gathers the original physical inputs, sums over exactly N keys and D features, is noncausal, and retains the exact decimal coefficient and BN-dependent bias indexing. Its denominator is positive whenever N>0. Real semantics erase rounding; no accuracy or exact native-to-Real identity follows.
independent_Real_review.connection: Real.answer_real proves the online recurrence against RealMath.expected; RealReturned.target_at_program connects the program/lane coordinates to the independent logical target. Actual Tensor addressing and bias_read connect the same physical reader to every valid logical operand. The public result combines this with derived full-grid success and output readback.
independent_Real_review.non_circularity: mathematicalTarget reaches the independent finite-sum formula, not Whole.answer, Source.accumulated, Source.update, runPrograms or FP.Structural.exec. The saved public audit checks these exclusions.

independent_native_review.target: Specification.algorithm is a separately written state-free recurrence over original physical input words. It explicitly retains masked operands, scaled-and-narrowed query, storage bias add/multiply, QK and PV inputs, maximum/sum reductions, probability narrowing, online rescaling, final division and output cast. Binding.source_algorithm proves each operand and update connection before identifying the complete recurrence.
independent_native_review.one_model: The endpoint takes one Instructions record containing literal conversion, scalar unary/binary/ternary operations and one coordinate of a fixed seeded m16n8k16 instruction. Raw-word leaves use identity bits. There is no arbitrary-size dot, whole reduction, softmax, full output or execution-equivalence port. The optional historical two-model LocalTransport theorem is not a premise of the new endpoint.
independent_native_review.native_structure: Native.lower retains the compiler-style bias seed for QK, the rescaled live accumulator seed for PV, fixed increasing K16 instruction chunks, FP16/BF16 conversions, storage bias arithmetic, exp2, normalizer FMA, full division and final storage narrowing. Finite reduction trees, shuffles/shared routes and owner selection remain explicit. CompilerPlan contains finite configuration and integer routing identities, not graph evaluation or result equalities.
independent_native_review.word_domain: Original two-byte words, including NaNs and infinities, remain in the structural input domain. Final nativeReference returns the lower 16 bits after the explicit output-storage conversion under the same instruction model.
independent_native_review.non_circularity: nativeReference and nativeTarget avoid source execution, Whole.answer, Source.accumulated and Source.update, as checked in the saved audit. Their shared algebra/instruction model is the declared local boundary, not an assumed complete algorithm result.
independent_native_review.conformance_boundary: The theorem does not verify the compiler, driver, ISA implementation or numerical accuracy. Applicability of the selected compiler layout and scalar/conversion/instruction interpretation remains an explicit boundary. This review does not reinterpret those boundaries as pending numerical experiments.

Tensor_and_frame_review.shared_input_identity: All roles use original object/storage metadata and one physical address reader. Legal input aliases therefore share values without snapshots or private arrays. actual_address derives pointer-plus-stride equality from capacity, inBounds and pointer laws; actual_read and bias_read provide the corresponding logical Tensor reads.
Tensor_and_frame_review.tagged_source_frame: RawFrame is proved for every source region and offset outside actual logical stores, including output-view gaps. It follows from the complete source store frame and grid coverage, rather than being assumed in admission.
Tensor_and_frame_review.physical_observation: observe is the explicitly declared mathematical observation of source output words at original Out addresses, retaining the previous reader elsewhere. observe_store is connected to the derived final source memory. The exterior frame is paired with that genuine source RawFrame; it is not claimed to implement a host allocator, copyback or unified final byteheap.
Tensor_and_frame_review.read_allocations: read_exterior uses checked whole-allocation separation and actual_address to preserve every logical input read. backing_exterior covers every address in each read allocation, including prefixes, gaps and trailing storage. Native output decoding uses the compiler-selected owner for each logical output dimension; exterior/read frames hold for every owner.

Selected Python, guards, Kernels.lean and all original task proof bodies are preserved.

build_and_preservation_review.cache_boundary: Only the 39 listed task modules have fresh source-current build receipts here. Other repository core and package caches were reused. Import/hash checks and current API probes do not amount to a fresh whole-core or cold-cache rebuild certification.

saved_validation_review.host_and_address_controls: The unchanged checker reports 49 metadata/host cases plus six signed scalar-word controls, totaling 55, seven complete address-grid enumerations and six historical original-source counterexamples. Its harness executes the actual wrapper against a metadata facade and captures its launch; its independent address enumerator checks logical coverage, collisions, frames and bounds. These are saved host/address controls, not GPU numerical evidence.
saved_validation_review.actual_binder: Ten offline SM80 profiles use Triton 3.7.1 create_function_from_signature/native specialization and _pack_args on actual CPU Tensor descriptors. This harness constructs the wrapper-aligned arguments directly; it is not an actual CUDA launch or wrapper execution. The source has 35 arguments and six explicit constexpr parameters. Independently reconstructed exact source order, every saved signature, constant and divisibility attribute: four unit strides specialize to constexpr 1, N_CTX=1 additionally specializes in the singleton profiles, scale is fp32 and P_SEQ=0 remains runtime i32 with divisibility 16. Warp/stage/fusion options match the source configuration.
saved_validation_review.compiler_profiles: Each dtype has [N,D,BM,BN,warps,stages] equal to [1,16,16,16,8,4], [129,128,128,128,4,4], [129,128,128,128,8,4], [97,64,128,16,4,1] and [65,32,16,128,8,4]. All ten saved records reached static compilation and have TTIR, TTGIR, LLVM and PTX artifacts.
saved_validation_review.artifact_multiplicity: Forty saved text paths contain eight distinct TTIR contents and ten distinct contents in each of TTGIR, LLVM and PTX, for 38 distinct text artifacts. The four/eight-warp D128 pairs share TTIR but differ in later lowering.
saved_validation_review.compiler_observations: All ten TTIR profiles retain the query widening/narrowing, storage bias add/multiply/widening, two storage-by-storage FP32 dots, probability storage cast and final storage cast/store. TTGIR connects QK to widened storage bias and PV to the rescaled live accumulator. Saved SM80 PTX/LLVM contain fixed m16n8k16 FP16/BF16 instructions, ex2.approx.ftz.f32, div.full.f32 and FP32 FMA. FP16 bias uses half add/multiply; BF16 bias uses BF16 FMA. The generic TTIR/TTGIR inputPrecision=tf32 attribute does not imply TF32 operands: the actual operands and PTX instructions are FP16/BF16, with no TF32 MMA.
saved_validation_review.CPU_complete_cases: The saved actual Triton CPU interpreter executes four FP16 cases: [1,1,1,16], [1,2,17,16], [2,2,65,32] and [1,2,129,16], with multiple heads/batches, independent pitches, storage offset five, prefix/gap/tail backing and query/key tails. These shapes imply 35 full-grid programs and 13008 logical output elements; those counts were reconstructed arithmetically from saved records, not obtained by a review rerun.
saved_validation_review.CPU_reference_and_frame: The finite controls use Q=K=bias=0 and V=2, with scale 0.125. They check every logical output equals exactly 2, compare the entire gapped output backing against the expected backing and verify all input backings and bias remain unchanged. The actual wrapper returns None. Real CPU Torch storage is wrapped in a Tensor subclass whose device property and module Tensor classification/context provide CUDA metadata; this is not real CUDA execution or a general instruction-conformance experiment.
saved_validation_review.CPU_empty_and_BF16_boundary: Six empty controls cover B=0, H=0 and N=0 in each dtype. Nonempty BF16 is not counted: the initial saved run fails at the bias scalar operation because InterpreterBuilder.get_bf16 is absent. The initial script/log are retained. The final harness differs only by skipping nonempty BF16 and adding explicit reporting of that limitation; no interpreter/backend workaround or source modification was applied.
saved_validation_review.no_review_rerun: The reviewer ran only a read-only saved-evidence verifier and independent JSON/hash/AST/import/arithmetic/IR-text checks. No Lean compiler, Triton compiler, host harness, CPU interpreter, GPU or kernel execution was rerun.

resource_applicability_review.official_basis: The pinned CUDA 12.6.3 programming-guide excerpt specifies 163 KiB per block for compute capability 8.0/8.7.
resource_applicability_review.inapplicable_profiles: For each storage dtype, [N,D,BM,BN]=[129,128,128,128] with four warps/four stages requests 231424 shared bytes and eight warps/four stages requests 229632. All four exceed the SM80 per-block bound despite successful static compilation.
resource_applicability_review.other_profiles: The remaining six request 1568, 22528 or 54272 bytes, below this single shared-memory bound. That comparison alone establishes no runtime-success or general resource claim.
resource_applicability_review.classification: The packet and unchanged wrapper declare compiler configuration applicability, driver and device resources as external runtime conditions. These four saved profiles are therefore inapplicable SM80 profiles, not a newly diagnosed source/mathematical defect or an unfulfilled numerical-experiment requirement. No stronger guard was introduced and no universal GPU/resource claim is accepted.

nonblocking_observations.observation: The unchanged checker emits a fixed source-binding boundary sentence saying 'all eight offline profiles'. The generated profiles array contains ten checked entries, its log says PASS 10 profiles, and delivery/README/validation correctly report ten. This stale sentence is not evidence for a different count; the independently verified count is ten.

The unchanged host checker prints 'floating instruction validation is deferred'. Delivery and README explicitly identify this as historical wording superseded for the new one-model endpoint by numerical-obligations.json. The new endpoint has no numerical transport premise or pending numerical experiment; it also makes no GPU or native-to-Real accuracy claim.
